Compute Odds Ratios

Source: R/oddsRatio.R
oddsRatio.Rd

Computes odds ratios for 2x2 contingency tables or binomial generalized linear models.

oddsRatio(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
oddsRatio(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  conf.level = NA,
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  method = c("wald", "exact", "midp"),
  interval = c(0, 1000),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'glm'
oddsRatio(
  x,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  method = c("wald", "profile"),
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'OddsRatio'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

an object for which odds ratios should be computed

...

further arguments passed to methods

y

optional second variable. If supplied, table(x, y, ...) is computed.

conf.level

confidence level for interval estimation. If NA, only the point estimate is returned.

sides

type of confidence interval. One of "two.sided", "left", or "right".

method

character string specifying the interval method. One of "wald" or "profile".

interval

numeric vector of length two specifying the search interval used by the mid-p method

digits

number of digits used for printing

Value

the returned value depends on the input. For contingency tables, conf.level = NA yields a numeric scalar; otherwise the result is a named numeric vector with elements:

est

odds ratio estimate

lci

lower confidence interval bound

uci

upper confidence interval bound

For binomial generalized linear models, an object of class "OddsRatio" is returned.

Details

For contingency tables, the function returns the odds ratio together with optional confidence intervals. For binomial generalized linear models, exponentiated regression coefficients together with confidence intervals are returned.

For 2x2 contingency tables, the odds ratio is defined as:

$$ OR = \frac{n_{11} n_{22}}{n_{12} n_{21}} $$

The following confidence interval methods are available:

  • "wald" Asymptotic Wald interval.

  • "exact" Fisher exact interval.

  • "midp" Median unbiased mid-p interval.

For generalized linear models, exponentiated regression coefficients are reported together with Wald or profile likelihood confidence intervals.

Note

No short alias is exported by default to avoid conflicts with rlang and base R naming conventions. Call attachAliases() once per session (or script) to make or() available as a convenient shorthand.

References

Agresti, A. (2013). Categorical Data Analysis (3rd ed.). Wiley.

Fisher, R. A. (1935). The logic of inductive inference. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, 98(1), 39–82.

Gart, J. J. (1966). Alternative analyses of contingency tables. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, 28(1), 164–179.

See also

attachAliases

Other effect.size: cohenD(), cohenH(), etaSq(), glassDelta(), relRisk()

Examples

# 2x2 contingency table
tab <- matrix(
  c(10, 20,
    5, 30),
  nrow = 2
)

oddsRatio(tab)
#> [1] 3

oddsRatio(
  tab,
  conf.level = 0.95
)
#>        est        lci        uci 
#>  3.0000000  0.8914747 10.0956314 


# logistic regression
fit <- glm(
  vs ~ am,
  data = mtcars,
  family = binomial
)

oddsRatio(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> glm(formula = vs ~ am, family = binomial, data = mtcars)
#> 
#> Odds Ratios (95% two.sided CI, method = wald):
#> 
#>               est   lci   uci pValue
#> (Intercept) 0.583 0.230 1.482  0.257
#> am          2.000 0.476 8.395  0.344
#>
